subject: general
question: Which of the following is an overhead expense in a production cost?
solution:
The correct answer is Insurance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The ongoing costs associated with maintaining a business are known as overhead or overhead charges in the business sector.**** **Unlike operating expenses like raw materials and labour, overheads cannot easily be linked to or recognised with any one revenue unit.
 
• **All costs on the income statement other than direct labour, direct supplies, and direct expenses are referred to as overhead expenses.**
 
• Accounting fees, advertising, **insurance**, interest, legal fees, labour costs, rent, repairs, supplies, taxes, phone bills, travel expenses, and utilities are **examples of overhead costs.**
 
• **Indirect expenses and fixed costs, two accounting concepts, are frequently linked to overheads.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Labour**

 
 
• **A labourer (or labourer) is a person employed in the construction industry who does manual labour.** Workers are members of a working-class who only own their labour as a significant tangible possession.
 
 **Raw materials** ​

 
 
• **Materials or substances used in the initial stages of producing or manufacturing items are known as raw materials.**
 
• On commodity exchanges around the world,** raw materials are commodities that are purchased and sold. **Because raw materials are production factors, businesses trade them on the factor market.
 
 
 
• **Consumable manufacturing supplies**
 
 
• **​Consumable materials include things like solder that are used up during production** but do not include things like the **packaging for finished goods, labels, skids, pallets, or shipping packing materials.**
